architecture_boilerplate.text:
This binder describes the fixed AIC Server enclave model used for assessment packaging.

The control plane includes sign-in, privileged access, inventory, Current State Compliance, the Assessment Binder, disclosures, and Secure Share. Managed machines use agents when enroled. Agentless discovery is used where supported. System Groups set sampling scope. Remote Access / Connect records operator sessions on assigned workstations.

Organisation fields (legal name, CAGE, enclave name, MSP) fill this instance. They do not change the product model.

Typical deployments run in cloud infrastructure (AIC-operated or customer tenant). On-premises partner models may apply. AIC usually does not keep standing login access to customer hosts. Day-to-day work uses product roles, justifications, and evidence citations.

Cite live compliance scans, inventory, System Groups, Secure Share citations (titles and ids only - no CUI document bodies), Connect recordings, crypto status, disclosures, and retests. Do not treat this narrative alone as proof. Lab SoftHSM and demo passwords are not production claims.

First-pass packaging covers CMMC Levels 1 - 3 and related NIST SP 800-171 / 800-172 needs. NIST SP 800-53 remains the security design floor.

Cloud SKUs target FedRAMP and Microsoft GCC High postures where selected. This text does not claim a current FedRAMP ATO. Assessor sign-off lines stay blank in this tool. An assessor will decide Met after evidence review. This text alone does not mark a control Met.

explanation.text: CMMC (32 CFR 170) is DoD assessment packaging over NIST SP 800-171 (and, at Level 3, selected NIST SP 800-172 enhanced requirements). Level 1 covers basic FCI safeguarding; Level 2 aligns to the 110 800-171 Rev 2 practices for CUI; Level 3 adds enhanced 800-172 requirements. CMMC does not replace the NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control design floor — it packages assessment evidence for a C3PAO / DoD review.

NIST SP 800–171 Rev 2 defines 110 security requirements in 14 families for protecting CUI in non-federal systems. Level 1 packaging focuses on basic / FCI-oriented practices; Level 2 is the full 110-practice set commonly paired with CMMC Level 2; Level 3 framing may reference additional enhanced expectations. Product control design still follows the NIST SP 800–53 Rev 5 floor; 800–171 is assessment packaging over that floor.

NIST SP 800-172 (Feb 2021) adds 35 enhanced security requirements beyond 800-171. CMMC Level 3 selects a subset of these. This packaging view emphasizes enhanced requirements together with the underlying 800-171 / CMMC evidence. Unproven enhanced claims stay gap or unknown — switching here filters/remaps scope; it does not invent new host evidence.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 is the control design floor for this product (moderate baseline, with High where selected). Control families (AC, AU, CM, IA, SC, SI, and others) organize the catalogue. CMMC / 800-171 / 800-172 rows elsewhere are assessment packaging overlays that reuse the same enclave evidence — they are not a thinner substitute for the 800-53 floor.
